morph.note: Present of √कृ, eighth class (कर-उ-मि → करोमि). The present in a deliberative question: ‘what am I to do?’.
Past participle of आ + √लोच् (tenth class, so -इत: आलोचित) negated with अन्- before the vowel. It echoes अल्पबुद्धित्वात् of 5.119.
Nominative singular of the in-stem बलिन् ‘having strength’: the n is lost and the i lengthened (बली).

mantras.anvaya: एतत् एवम् (अस्ति): शुम्भः बली, निशुम्भः च अतिवीर्यवान्। किं करोमि? यत् मे प्रतिज्ञा पुरा अनालोचिता (कृता)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A concession (एवम् एतत्) spelled out in two nominal sentences; a deliberative question; a causal clause (यत् …) giving the reason.
mantras.lit: This is so: Śumbha is strong, and Niśumbha exceedingly valiant. What can I do, since my vow (was made) long ago without reflection?
mantras.tr: It is just as you say: Śumbha is mighty, and Niśumbha of surpassing valour. But what can I do? My vow was made long ago, without thought.

comm.t: The Devī concedes the messenger’s point about the brothers’ strength, as she did at first (5.118), and again pleads her old vow: she cannot set it aside.

The mock-helplessness (किं करोमि) and the claim that the vow was ill-considered (अनालोचिता) repeat the irony of 5.119. The vow cannot be broken, so the only way to her hand is through battle — which is the outcome she intends.

Variant: for निशुम्भश्चातिवीर्यवान् the GRETIL Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa and Freund read निशुम्भश्चापि तादृशः, the phrase the Devī used in 5.118. The Gita Press reading is kept here; the variant does not change the sense.

flags.uncertain: Textual variant (corrections.json, status ‘Textual Verification Required’): Gita Press निशुम्भश्चातिवीर्यवान्, other witnesses निशुम्भश्चापि तादृशः. The analysis follows the Gita Press text.

samasa.literal: to the Indra (chief) of the asuras
samasa.sense: to Śumbha, king of the asuras

morph.note: Imperative ātmanepada of आ + √चक्ष्: चक्ष् + स्व, with the s lost between consonants (चक्ष्व). ‘Tell, report’.
Past participle of आ + √दृ; besides ‘honoured’ it means ‘attentive, careful’, an active sense. Here it describes the messenger: report it all faithfully.
Third-person imperative of √कृ: ‘let him do’. The Devī leaves the decision — and so the war — to Śumbha.

mantras.anvaya: सः त्वं गच्छ। मया ते यत् एतत् सर्वम् उक्तम्, तत् आदृतः (सन्) असुरेन्द्राय आचक्ष्व; सः च यत् युक्तं तत् करोतु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two imperatives addressed to the messenger (गच्छ, आचक्ष्व), the second with a relative pair (यत् … तत्) as its object; then a third-person imperative (करोतु) for Śumbha.
mantras.lit: So go, you; all this that has been said to you by me, report that with care to the lord of the asuras; and let him do that which is fitting.
mantras.tr: Go, then, and tell the lord of the asuras faithfully all that I have said to you; and let him do whatever he thinks fit.
mantras.tr_note: युक्तम् ‘what is fitting’ is rendered ‘whatever he thinks fit’, the usual sense of the formula.

comm.t: The Devī dismisses the messenger: he is to report her words exactly to Śumbha, and Śumbha must decide. The chapter ends here; the next opens with the messenger’s report and Śumbha’s anger (6.2–3).

The formula ‘let him do what is fitting’ courteously leaves the choice to the enemy, but the vow has already determined it: he can win her only in battle. In the Gita Press pāṭha the chapter’s last mantra is followed by the bīja ॐ, which belongs to the recitation, not to the Purāṇa, and the colophon names the chapter देव्या दूतसंवादः, ‘the Devī’s dialogue with the messenger’.
